- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates true price drops after strong prior declines; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for 3–5 day horizons.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is neutral or rising.
- When sentiment history shows a clear reversal (e.g., from high to low), model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–2% downward correction to forecast 2–3 days ahead.
